I turned off Wi-Fi Calling like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all these steps.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message to my daughter, but it just won’t go through. I’m not very good with these things, so I’m hoping you can help me fix it.

I can help you with that! To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide either your phone number, your full name and date of birth, or your customer ID? This will help me look up your account and assist you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

Thank you for providing your information. To help you send picture messages (MMS), I’ll need to check a few things on your phone and account. 

Could you please let me know if you’re having trouble sending picture messages from the phone number 555-123-2002, or is it a different number on your account? This will help me troubleshoot the correct line.
Yes, it’s the number 555-123-2002 that I’m having trouble with. That’s the phone I use, and I can’t send picture messages from it.

Thank you for confirming. To help you fix the issue with sending picture messages, I’ll guide you through a few quick checks on your phone. 

First, could you please check if you can make regular calls and if your mobile data (internet) is working on your phone? This will help us determine if the problem is with your service or just with picture messaging.

I’m not sure how to check if my mobile data is working. I can make regular calls just fine, but I don’t really know how to tell if the internet is working on my phone. Could you tell me how to check that?

No problem! Here’s a simple way to check if your mobile data (internet) is working:

1. Make sure you are not connected to Wi-Fi (turn off Wi-Fi if it’s on).
2. Open your web browser (like Chrome or Safari) on your phone.
3. Try to visit any website, such as www.google.com.

If the website loads, your mobile data is working. If it doesn’t load and you see an error, your mobile data might not be working.

Could you please try this and let me know what happens?
Wi-Fi is turned OFF.

Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: connected
Cellular Signal: poor
Cellular Network Type: 2G
Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No

I checked, and my Wi-Fi is turned off. My phone says it’s connected to the mobile network, but the signal looks pretty weak and it says something about 2G. Does that mean my internet isn’t working properly? I’m not sure what to do next.

Thank you for checking. If your phone is showing a 2G connection and a weak signal, that could definitely cause problems with sending picture messages (MMS), as 2G networks are generally not suitable for MMS or fast internet.

To improve this, you’ll need to change your phone’s network mode to prefer 4G or 5G, which will give you better data speeds and should help with sending picture messages.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to change your network mode to 4G/5G on your phone? If so, please let me know what type of phone you have (Android or iPhone), and I’ll guide you through the process.
Network Mode Preference: 2g_only

Oh, it looks like my phone is set to use only 2G right now. I’m not sure how that happened. I have an Android phone, but I get confused easily with these settings. Could you please give me very simple, step-by-step instructions to change it to 4G or 5G? I’m worried I might mess something up.

Of course! I’ll give you simple, step-by-step instructions to change your network mode to 4G or 5G on your Android phone. Please follow these steps:

1. Open the “Settings” app on your phone.
2. Scroll down and tap on “Connections” or “Network & Internet” (the name may vary depending on your phone).
3. Tap on “Mobile networks.”
4. Tap on “Preferred network type” or “Network mode.”
5. You’ll see options like “2G,” “3G,” “4G,” or “5G.” Select “4G/5G (auto)” or “4G/3G/2G (auto connect)” if available.
6. Once selected, exit the settings.

After you do this, your phone should try to connect to a faster network. Wait a minute and check if your signal improves and if you see “4G” or “5G” at the top of your screen.

Please let me know once you’ve done this, or if you need help with any of the steps!

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I followed your instructions and now I see “5G” at the top of my screen, and the signal looks much better. What should I do next? Should I try sending a picture message again?

That’s great! Yes, please try sending a picture message to your daughter again now that your phone is connected to 5G with a stronger signal.

Let me know if the picture message goes through successfully, or if you still have trouble sending it. If it doesn’t work, I’ll help you with the next steps.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I just tried to send a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. It’s really frustrating—why isn’t it working even though the signal is better now?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your signal and network mode are now correct, the next step is to check your phone’s settings for sending picture messages (MMS). Sometimes, incorrect settings can prevent MMS from working.

Could you please check your phone’s Access Point Name (APN) settings? This is a technical setting that controls how your phone connects to our network for internet and MMS. 

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to check your APN settings, or do you see an option for “Access Point Names” or “APN” in your phone’s Mobile Network settings?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I found something called “APN Name” and it says “internet.” There’s also something about an “MMSC URL” that looks like a web address. I’m not sure if these are correct or if I need to change anything. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking your APN settings. Sometimes, even if the APN name looks correct, the MMSC URL or other details might not be set up properly, which can cause issues with sending picture messages.

The best way to fix this is to reset your APN settings to the default values provided by your carrier. Here’s how you can do that on your Android phone:

1. Go to “Settings.”
2. Tap on “Connections” or “Network & Internet.”
3. Tap on “Mobile networks.”
4. Tap on “Access Point Names” or “APN.”
5. Look for an option that says “Reset to default” or “Reset settings.” Tap on it to reset your APN settings.

After you reset the APN settings, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Please let me know once you’ve reset your APN settings and restarted your phone, or if you need help with any of the steps.

APN settings will reset at reboot.

I found the option to reset the APN settings, and I tapped it. It says the settings will reset when I restart my phone. But I’m a bit nervous—if I restart, will I lose any of my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important.

Rest assured, restarting your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, or other personal data. It simply turns your phone off and back on, which helps apply the new network settings.

You can safely restart your phone now. Once it’s back on, try sending a picture message again. If you need help with restarting your phone, let me know!

1. Is your mobile data turned ON (not just Wi-Fi)?
2. Is Data Saver mode turned OFF?
3. Is Wi-Fi Calling turned OFF?
4. Does your messaging app have permission to access storage and SMS?

Could you please check if your mobile data is ON and if Data Saver mode is OFF? If you’re not sure how to check these, I can guide you step by step. Let me know which one you’d like to check first, or if you want help with all of them.

Great, thank you for checking those settings. Next, let’s check if Wi-Fi Calling is turned ON, as this can sometimes interfere with sending picture messages (MMS).

Could you please check your phone’s settings for Wi-Fi Calling? If you’re not sure how to do this, I can provide step-by-step instructions for checking and turning off Wi-Fi Calling on your Android phone. Would you like those instructions?
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
It looks like Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON. Should I turn it off? Will that help with sending picture messages? I’m not sure what Wi-Fi Calling even does.

Yes, please turn Wi-Fi Calling OFF. Sometimes, having Wi-Fi Calling enabled can interfere with sending picture messages (MMS), especially if your carrier doesn’t support MMS over Wi-Fi.

Turning it off will not affect your ability to make regular calls or use your phone normally—it just means your calls will go over the mobile network instead of Wi-Fi.

After you turn off Wi-Fi Calling, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you still have trouble.

Since you’ve tried all the main troubleshooting steps—network mode, APN reset, mobile data, Data Saver, and Wi-Fi Calling—and the issue still isn’t resolved, there may be a more complex technical problem with your account or device that requires advanced support.
